title: Chiton
description: Find the lowest-risk path through a cave grid using Dijkstra's algorithm.
writeup:
## Approach

This is a shortest-path problem on a weighted grid. Each cell's value is the cost to enter it. Dijkstra's algorithm with a min-heap finds the optimal path from top-left to bottom-right.

## Part 1

Run Dijkstra on the original grid. The priority queue processes cells in order of cumulative risk. Early termination fires as soon as the bottom-right corner is popped.

## Part 2

The grid tiles 5× in each direction. Each tile's risk values are the original values incremented by the tile's Manhattan distance from the origin, wrapping 9 → 1 (not 0). Build the expanded grid, then run the same Dijkstra. The 5× expansion makes the grid 25× larger, but Dijkstra with a binary heap handles it efficiently in O(n log n).
